events.title: Mt.Gox files for bankruptcy in Japan after hack
events.description: Mt. Gox, once the world’s biggest bitcoin exchange, filed for bankruptcy protection in Japan, saying it may have lost nearly half a billion dollars worth of the virtual coin due to hacking into its faulty computer system. Lawsuits were filed.

events.description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approves Bitcoin futures ETFs for the first time in history, opening up the cryptocurrency to the masses and allowing investors exposure to Bitcoin in an alternative, more regulated form.

events.title: Joe Biden signs bill to regulate  crypto transactions
events.description: US President Joe Biden sign a $1.2 trillion infrastructure bill which include some crypto regulation. The bill specifically asks that CeFi exchanges notify the IRS of any and all crypto transactions, similar to how traditional stockbrokers have to the supply details of who’s buying stocks and shares.

events.title: Kazakhstan Bitcoin mining shuts  down
events.description: A decision by the government  to remove energy price caps causes Bitcoin mining costs to surge and protests to break out. After four days of rioting, on January 6, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev blocks all internet access across Kazakhstan, ending Bitcoin mining in the world's second-biggest mining hub.

events.title: Joe Biden signs executive order titled "Ensuring Responsible Development of Digital Assets"

events.title: The Terra network starts crashing
events.description: The Terra network, one of crypto’s biggest success stories in 2021, starts coming apart at the seams. The Luna token loses 96% of its value within 24 hours and the UST stablecoin depegs, dropping from $1 to $0.30.

events.title: Celsius network freezes customer withdrawals, swaps and transfers

Rumours then spread that the firm has secretly slipped into insolvency and is trying to make off with its customers’ cash.

events.title: Celsius files for bankrupcy
